title: Sponsored hiring: a public, quarterly window into headcount growth
what: Every quarter Exponent asks the US Department of Labor for permission to employ foreign specialists (H-1B applications) or sponsor their green cards (PERM). Those filings are public - employer, job title, worksite, wage level - and for a PhD-heavy firm they are a real slice of hiring activity, published quarterly while total headcount only appears in filings.
how: We downloaded the DOL's official disclosure files (~1.2GB, every US employer's filings) and filtered to Exponent, Inc. An H-1B filing signals hiring intent for a specialist role; a PERM filing signals a long-term retention commitment to a scientist already on staff.
thesis: Thesis trigger 1 needs headcount GROWING. The company confirmed +5% in Q1-2026; this feed is the between-quarters check that the hiring engine keeps running - and the job titles show WHERE the growth is (batteries, data science, biomedical engineering = proactive-segment capacity).
caveats: This is only the sponsored-hire slice of total hiring - read it as a direction and mix signal, not a census.
LCA filings include renewals and transfers, not just new hires.
DOL publishes with a lag; the newest quarter is always incomplete.
